memory_candidates: In this Lean4/Mathlib setup, `List.mem_cons`+`List.mem_append` applied via `simp only` to `x ∈ a :: (l1 ++ l2)` produces a LEFT-associated disjunction `(x = a ∨ x ∈ l1) ∨ x ∈ l2`, not right-associated. `rcases h with rfl | h1 | h2` silently mis-splits (tries to subst the whole inl compound); use `rcases h with (rfl | h1) | h2` instead.

`split` tactic on a goal shaped `match (bigExpr).fst with | RuleResultCtor => ...` prefers to split on the OUTER match (over the result's own constructor, introducing an opaque equation hypothesis) rather than descending into `bigExpr`'s own internal match/if — even after `dsimp only` reduces `bigExpr` to a clean `if`/`match`. To target the inner conditional, use `by_cases`/`rcases ... with` explicitly on the inner discriminant instead of relying on `split` to find it.

Lean's `omega` occasionally fails on trivially-true goals (`w ≤ B ⊢ w < B + 1`) inside `have h := by omega` when embedded inside certain anonymous-constructor/tactic-block positions in this codebase (root cause not fully diagnosed — possibly elaboration-order/metavariable postponement related to nested `refine`/`exact ⟨_, by omega, _⟩`). When `omega` inexplicably fails on an obviously-true Nat goal, fall back to explicit lemmas (`Nat.lt_succ_of_le`, `Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp`) which are unaffected.
